findings.issue: This is the test at line 1503. Prompt 179:66-70 changes it to use a synthetic roster of 44 manifests at `candidate=1.5.0` and says "preserve os demais asserts". One of the preserved asserts is the `PUBLICATION_VERSION_DRIFT` negative at lines 1520-1525. It mutates `packages[0].manifest.version` to the literal `'1.5.0'` and expects `validatePublicationRoster(..., candidate)` to throw. Once the candidate is `1.5.0`, the mutated entry equals the candidate. `validatePublicationRoster` (scripts/lib/publication-dist-tag.mjs:44-47) then accepts it and `assert.throws` fails. That is a second red before the marker, and it stays red after the marker. It breaks the rule in contract:164-169 and prompt 179:84-88 that only the renamed test 345 may be red. The Inspector again has to make a semantic decision that neither the contract nor the prompt made. The other asserts hold with a stable candidate. I checked the code: `mutableTag=latest`, so `rc=rc.2` still gives `PUBLICATION_DIST_TAG_UNKNOWN` and `rc=1.5.0-rc.0` still gives `PUBLICATION_DIST_TAG_DRIFT`.
findings.required_change: In prompt 179:64-71 and contract §Sensores:156-163, state that the version-drift negative must use a version different from the candidate. The recommended value is `'1.5.0-rc.3'`, the workspace version that must not be published. `previousCandidate` (`'1.5.0-rc.2'`) would also work. State as well that the only removals are the lines that derive `candidate`/`previousCandidate` from the root `package.json` (1507-1510) and the `every(manifest.version === candidate)` over real manifests (1514). With those removals, all other asserts stay intact, and that counts as a re-oracle, not a weakening.

findings.issue: The prompt does not say whether the test title 'current RC publication roster, old rc visibility, bounded rereads, and stable-only release tags' should be renamed to reflect the stable candidate. It also does not require a positive post-publication case (`latest=1.5.0`, `rc=1.5.0-rc.2` unchanged → no throw) in the same test. Because the title is the key in `law/trace.json`, an implicit rename by the Inspector would change what the Architect has to rebind.
findings.required_change: Pick one: either keep the title (so the trace key stays stable), or rename it explicitly (for example 'final stable publication roster, rc2 visibility, bounded rereads, and stable release tags'). Optionally add the positive `verifyPostPublishDistTags` case with `latest=1.5.0`.

summary: Cycle 2 is mostly resolved. (1) The contract (§Sensores:156-163) and prompt 179 (64-71) turn the test at line 1503 into a proof for the stable candidate. It takes `1.5.0` from the policy, uses a synthetic roster of 44 packages for order, the angular canary and rereads, and keeps `previousCandidate=rc.2`. It does not read an RC version from the root manifest, accepts `v1.5.0` and rejects `v1.5.0-rc.2`. Equality with the real workspace stays only in the renamed test 345, which is the only expected red before the marker. (2) `markerCommits` is fully specified as `rev-list --first-parent --reverse base..head` with {sha,subject} (contract:138-139; 179:31-32; 180:32-33). `packageStates` reuses the existing shape {name,manifestPath,baseVersion,candidateVersion} with 44 `baseVersion=1.5.0-rc.3` taken from origin/main. That matches `isVersionedPreModeCandidate` (release-context.mjs:130-198) and the construction in run-release-preparation.mjs:109-137. (3) The marker parent's pre state must be structurally equal to origin/main's `pre.json`, including `initialVersions` and `changesets` (contract:38-41; 180:31-32), and prompt 179:34-36 adds the drift negative. One blocker remains: the instruction to preserve the other asserts, combined with the stable `1.5.0` candidate, makes the `PUBLICATION_VERSION_DRIFT` negative, which mutates to the literal `'1.5.0'`, stop throwing. That produces an unplanned red. It is a one-line fix in the prompt and contract, and once it is applied the set is ready for PASS. This review is read-only. I ran no Git command, and it does not release the Inspector or Engineer, declare the release, open a PR or publish.
